Deuteronomy 9:10 And the Lord gave me the two tables of stone written with the finger of God, and on them there had been written all the words which the Lord spoke to you in the mountain in the day of the assembly.
Deuteronomy 9:11 And it came to pass after forty days and forty nights, the Lord gave me the two tables of stone, the tables of the covenant.
Deuteronomy 9:12 And the Lord said to me, Arise, go down quickly from hence, for thy people whom thou broughtest out of the land of Egypt have transgressed; they have gone aside quickly out of the way which I commanded them, and have made themselves a molten image.
Deuteronomy 9:13 And the Lord spoke to me, saying, I have spoken to thee once and again, saying, I have seen this people, and, behold, it is a stiff-necked people.

translations.T1:
that the Lord established with you. And I stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights; I did not eat bread or drink water.
<margin>10</margin> And the Lord gave me the two stone tablets written with the finger of God; and on them were written all the words that the Lord spoke to you on the mountain, on the day you were gathered together.
<margin>11</margin> And it happened after forty days and forty nights, the Lord gave me the two stone tablets, the tablets of the covenant.
<margin>12</margin> And the Lord said to me, "Arise and go down quickly from here, for your people whom you brought out of the land of Egypt have acted wickedly <note>original: "aϥaнoмєi", Greek: ἠνόμησεν</note>. They have turned aside <note>original: "aυpapaвa", Greek: παρέβησαν</note> quickly from the way that I commanded them; they have made for themselves a molten image."
<margin>13</margin> And the Lord said to me, "I have spoken to you once and twice, saying: 'I have seen this people, and behold, they are a stiff-necked <note>original: "naϣt мakϩ", translated as stubborn/stiff-necked</note> people.'
<margin>14</margin> Let me alone, so that I may destroy them and blot out their name from under heaven; and I will make you into a great and strong nation, and more numerous than these."

<summary>Moses recounts the Lord's instructions to descend the mountain after the people made a golden calf, and God's threat to destroy them and raise a new nation through Moses.</summary>

reference:
[context] Mark 6:13 They cast out many demons, and anointed many with oil who were sick, and healed them.
Mark 6:14 King Herod heard this, for his name had become known, and he said, 'John the Baptizer has risen from the dead, and therefore these powers are at work in him.'
Mark 6:15 But others said, 'He is Elijah.' Others said, 'He is a prophet, or like one of the prophets.'
Mark 6:16 But Herod, when he heard this, said, 'This is John, whom I beheaded. He has risen from the dead.'
Mark 6:17 For Herod himself had sent out and arrested John, and bound him in prison for the sake of Herodias, his brother Philip's wife, for he had married her.
Mark 6:18 For John said to Herod, 'It is not lawful for you to have your brother's wife.'
Mark 6:19 Herodias set herself against him, and desired to kill him, but she couldn't,
Mark 6:20 for Herod feared John, knowing that he was a righteous and holy man, and kept him safe. When he heard him, he did many things, and he heard him gladly.
[context] Mark 6:21 Then a convenient day came, that Herod on his birthday made a supper for his nobles, the high officers, and the chief men of Galilee.

It moves from the mission of the twelve apostles into the account of Herod’s reaction to Jesus' fame and the backstory of John the Baptist's imprisonment. The layout consists of the biblical text followed by a scholarly "critical apparatus" that compares various manuscripts.</meta>

<meta>This page continues the Sermon on the Mount from Matthew chapter 6, moving from the instructions on fasting to teachings on heavenly treasures and the "lamp of the body." It maintains the scholarly focus of Horner's edition, detailing minute dialectal and manuscript variations in the Bohairic Coptic tradition.</meta>

# ACCORDING TO MATTHEW

...for they disfigure their faces so that they may appear to men to be fasting.
Truly I say to you: they have received their reward.
<margin>22</margin> ¹⁷ But you, when you fast, anoint your head and wash your face. ¹⁸ So that you do not appear to men to be fasting, but to your Father who is in secret; and your Father who sees in secret shall reward you.

->12.<-
<note>This numeral "12" marks a traditional section or lesson division within the Coptic Gospel text.</note>

<margin>46 / 1</margin> <note>These marginal numbers refer to the Ammonian Sections (46) and Eusebian Canons (1), an ancient cross-referencing system for the Four Gospels.</note> ¹⁹ Do not lay up for yourselves treasures upon the earth, the place where moth and rust destroy, and the place where thieves dig through and steal.
²⁰ But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, the place where neither moth nor rust destroys, and where thieves do not dig through nor steal. ²¹ For where your treasure is, there also will your heart be.
<margin>47 / 5</margin> ²² The lamp of the body is the eye. If therefore your eye be single <note>The Coptic uses a loanword from the Greek "haplous," which means "simple," "sincere," or "single-focused," implying a heart undivided in its devotion to God.</note>, your whole body shall be full of light.
²³ But if your eye be evil, your whole body shall be full of darkness.
